stimulus.body: Ticket #3097 states: Der Build ist fehlgeschlagen. Das war unerwartet. The writer wants one sentence.

questions.stem: Which demonstrative pronoun can refer to the whole preceding sentence in a subordinate clause?

options.text: Use 'dieser' to refer only to a masculine noun.
Use 'das' to refer to the whole preceding sentence.
Use 'jener' to refer to a distant noun.
Use 'er' to refer to a masculine person.

questions.explanation: 'Das' can refer to a whole preceding clause or sentence, not just a noun. Other demonstratives target specific nouns.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A relative clause opened by a preposition
questions.learningObjective: Identify the case governed by a preposition opening a relative clause
questions.stem: In ticket #3311 the clause 'das Ticket, mit dem wir arbeiten' opens with 'mit'. Which case does it govern?

options.text: Use nominative because the pronoun is the subject.
Use accusative because 'mit' governs accusative.
Use genitive because 'mit' is a genitive preposition.
Use dative because 'mit' governs dative.

questions.explanation: 'Mit' governs dative, so the relative pronoun must be dative. The antecedent's gender shapes the base form only.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Word order in a subordinate clause with two verbs
questions.learningObjective: Explain verb order in a subordinate clause with a perfect auxiliary
questions.stem: Explain the order of participle and auxiliary in a perfect subordinate clause.

answer.exemplar: In a perfect subordinate clause the participle stands before the auxiliary at the end, as in 'weil er das getestet hat'.

questions.explanation: The finite auxiliary remains last in the subordinate clause, with the participle immediately before it. Main-clause order is wrong.
questions.hint: Participle before auxiliary at the end.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Word order in a subordinate clause with two verbs
questions.learningObjective: Order modal and infinitive in a subordinate clause
questions.stem: In ticket #3953 the clause 'weil er das lesen muss' contains an infinitive and a modal. Which order is correct?

options.text: Move the modal to second position after the subject.
options.misconception: applies main-clause order to subordinate clause

options.text: Put the modal first and the infinitive last.
Place both verbs before the object.
Put the infinitive first and the modal last.

questions.explanation: In a subordinate clause with a modal, the infinitive precedes the finite modal at the end. Main-clause order would put the modal second.
